statement: Let n = len(nums). For every pair of distinct edge indices i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(edges), deleting edges[i] and edges[j] from the tree splits the vertex set {0,...,n-1} into three nonempty connected components C1,C2,C3. For such a pair define score(i,j) = max(xor(C1), xor(C2), xor(C3)) - min(xor(C1), xor(C2), xor(C3)), where xor(C) is the bitwise XOR of nums[v] over all vertices v in C. The function returns a result r and r = min { score(i,j) : 0 <= i < j < len(edges) }.
preconditions: n = len(nums); 3 <= n <= 1000; 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000000 for every 0 <= i < n; len(edges) = n - 1; each edges[k] is a list of length 2 for 0 <= k < n - 1; edges[k][0] and edges[k][1] are distinct indices in [0,n); and the undirected simple graph on vertices 0,...,n-1 with edge set { {edges[k][0], edges[k][1]} : 0 <= k < n-1 } is a tree (connected and acyclic).
